system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Skylark Mobile's 30GB SIM-only plan, started 3 October 2026, has a 24-month minimum term at £22.00 a month including VAT. From April 2027 the price rises each April by a fixed £2.50 a month — the only rise during the term, notified 30 days ahead, and not a reason to cancel free. You get 30GB of UK data (no rollover; hotspot included), unlimited UK calls to 01, 02, 03 and 07 numbers (not 070 or 076) and unlimited texts. Calls to 084, 087, 09 and 118 numbers are included in your minutes, and 080 and 116 numbers are free. You can use your allowances in the Europe Zone (EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland) at no extra charge; outside it, roaming is £6 a day. You can set a spending cap of £0–£100 in the app; the default is £30. You can cancel within 14 days and pay only for what you've used; leaving later in the term means paying the remaining monthly charges less 4%, and after the term you can leave on 30 days' notice for free. Text PAC to 65075 or STAC to 75075 to switch. Loss of service unfixed after two working days earns £9.76 a day automatically, and unresolved complaints can go to the Communications Ombudsman after eight weeks.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
SKYLARK MOBILE — KEY CONTRACT INFORMATION AND SUMMARY OF TERMS Plan: Skylark 30GB SIM-only, 24-month minimum term. Contract start date: 3 October 2026.

1. Monthly charge. £22.00 per month, including VAT, for the 24-month minimum term, subject to the annual price change in section 2.

2. Annual price change. Each April, starting in April 2027, your monthly charge will increase by a fixed amount of £1.50 per month. This is the only price increase that will apply to your plan's monthly charge during the minimum term. We will remind you of the change at least 30 days in advance. Because this increase is set out in your contract, it does not give you a right to cancel without charge.

3. Allowances. Each month you get 30GB of UK data, unlimited UK calls to numbers starting 01, 02, 03 and 07 (excluding 070 and 076), and unlimited UK texts. Unused data does not roll over. Personal hotspot use is included within your data allowance.

4. Numbers not included. Calls to non-geographic numbers starting 084, 087, 09 and 118 are not included in your inclusive minutes and are charged at our access charge of 65p per minute plus the service charge set by the organisation you are calling. Calls to 080 and 116 numbers are free.

5. Roaming. Use of your allowances in our Europe Zone (EU countries, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland) is included at no extra charge, provided that over any four-month period you spend more days in the UK than abroad and use more of your allowance in the UK than abroad. If our records show that you have not met this condition, we will give you 14 days' notice, after which a surcharge of £2 per day of use abroad may apply until the pattern changes. Roaming outside the Europe Zone is charged at £6 per day.

6. Spending cap. You can set a monthly spending cap of between £0 and £100 for charges outside your allowance in the Skylark app. If you do not set one, the default cap is £30.

7. Cancelling. You can cancel within 14 days of the start date and pay only for the service used. After that, if you leave during the minimum term you must pay an early termination charge equal to the remaining monthly charges, less a 4% discount for not receiving the service. After the minimum term, you can leave with 30 days' notice and no charge.

8. Switching. To switch providers and keep your number, text "PAC" to 65075; to switch without keeping your number, text "STAC" to 75075. We will respond within one minute with the code and any charges due.

9. Service issues. If we fail to fix a total loss of service within two full working days of you reporting it, you are entitled to automatic compensation of £9.76 for each further day.

10. Complaints. If we cannot resolve your complaint within eight weeks, you may refer it to the Communications Ombudsman free of charge.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. What will my monthly charge be after the April 2027 price change?
2. What is the monthly charge before any price change?
3. Will a call to an 0871 customer-service number come out of my inclusive minutes?
4. I'm going to work in Spain for three and a half months, coming home for just two weeks in that period. Will roaming stay free the whole time?
response:
I checked each answer against the contract itself. My earlier notes had three errors, which are corrected below.

**1. Monthly charge after the April 2027 price change: £23.50**
The contract (section 2) sets a fixed rise of **£1.50** a month each April, so £22.00 becomes £23.50. My notes wrongly said £2.50. The charge rises by another £1.50 in April 2028, to £25.00. You'll be reminded at least 30 days before each rise. Because the rises are in the contract, they don't give you a right to cancel free.

**2. Monthly charge before any price change: £22.00**
This includes VAT (section 1).

**3. Will a call to an 0871 number use your inclusive minutes? No.**
0871 numbers fall under 087 numbers, which are **not included** in your minutes (section 4). You'll pay Skylark's access charge of **65p a minute**, plus a service charge set by the organisation you're calling. My notes wrongly said these calls were included. Only 080 and 116 numbers are free. It's worth checking whether the company has a free 080 number or a standard 01, 02 or 03 number you could call instead.

**4. Will roaming in Spain stay free the whole time? Probably not.**
My notes left out a condition in section 5. Spain is in the Europe Zone, but free use there only applies if, over any four-month period, you:
- spend more days in the UK than abroad, **and**
- use more of your allowance in the UK than abroad.

About 3½ months in Spain with only two weeks at home means far more days abroad than in the UK, so you won't meet this condition. If Skylark spots it, they'll give you **14 days' notice**. After that, a **£2 surcharge for each day you use your phone abroad** may apply until your usage pattern changes. The first part of your stay would probably be free, but the later weeks could cost about £14 a week. Your spending cap (£30 unless you've changed it) may limit these charges, so check your cap in the Skylark app before you go.

The other points in my notes match the contract.
